headline: Underwriting gains and record investment income lift profit
summary_short: W. R. Berkley's Q2 FY2026 net income rose 12.7% y/y to $452.3 million ($1.15 diluted EPS), as the GAAP combined ratio improved 1.6 points to 90.0% and operating ROE reached 20.5%.
summary_long: Operating income of $497.1 million (+18.2% y/y) was driven by outstanding underwriting performance and record net investment income of $418.7 million (+10.4% y/y), the latter reflecting growth in invested assets and a higher portfolio yield on fixed-maturity securities. The Insurance segment grew gross and net premiums written 5.4% and 3.7% to record levels, holding an 88.1% accident-year combined ratio excluding catastrophes. Total capital returned to shareholders was $334.1 million ($223M dividends, $111.5M buybacks). Common stockholders' equity rose to $9.833 billion and book value per share reached $26.50, up from $25.72 at year-end 2025. No explicit forward guidance was issued in the release.

drivers.explanation: CEO cited the quarter as "driven by outstanding underwriting performance and record net investment income," generating a 20.5% annualized operating ROE.
Attributed to higher underwriting income and record net investment income; partly tempered by a $55.2M pre-tax net investment loss vs. a $31.0M gain a year ago.
EPS growth (+15.0%) outpaced net income growth (+12.7%) because weighted diluted shares fell to 391.8M from 400.4M a year earlier via ongoing buybacks.
Attributed to outstanding underwriting performance, record net investment income, and Insurance segment premium growth to record levels under disciplined pricing.
Grew faster than operating income (+21.0% vs +18.2%) due to the same lower diluted share count from buybacks that lifted GAAP EPS.

Growth was muted by an $86.2M swing in net investment gains/losses (to a $55.2M loss from a $31.0M gain a year ago), offsetting most of the growth in premiums earned (+3.0%) and net investment income (+10.4%).
Company attributes the improvement to disciplined pricing and cycle management, which "resulted in a strong overall 88.1% accident year combined ratio, excluding catastrophe losses."
GAAP ROE fell to 18.6% (from 19.1%) even as operating ROE rose to 20.5% (from 20.0%), since GAAP net income includes this quarter's $55.2M pre-tax investment loss that operating income excludes.

Growth reflects retained earnings net of $334.1M capital returned to shareholders this quarter, reported net of $317M after-tax unrealized investment losses and $323M currency-translation losses embedded in equity as of June 30, 2026.
